findings.claim: The module never teaches a learner how to install the local PostgreSQL server and psql that the title, accepted intake and module lab require. The page begins with “You installed PostgreSQL,” relegates installation to “follow” an external download page, and checks only psql client availability; it does not give a standalone, supported-OS path to install/start the server, create or identify a connectable database, and verify the client-to-server connection. A beginner without PostgreSQL cannot reach objective o2 or the module lab from these instructions.
findings.recommendation: Keep the fixed topic and objectives, but add concise in-artifact macOS, Windows and Linux installation routes. Give each route a numbered four-part procedure: where to act, what to do, expected server/client output, and a completion check. End with a real psql connection plus SELECT version(); and route common service, role, database and authentication failures to specific recovery steps; do not rely on the optional external link for required instructions.

findings.claim: The lab claims objectives that require choosing a suitable design, data types and constraints, but the public test accepts only one representation (for example text rather than another suitable character type for students.email and courses.code), while README task lines 73-76 disclose those exact expected types, key shape, defaults and constraints so learners can transcribe them. The design is also pre-specified down to every table and column. This makes the lab reliably passable only by giving away the decisions it claims to elicit, rather than authentically assessing tables-keys-and-relationships o3, designing-tables-from-a-user-story o2, or CREATE TABLE o1/o2.
findings.recommendation: Keep the fixed user story, module scope and no-container local-PostgreSQL route. Make public tests accept behaviorally equivalent suitable types/default expressions and validate acceptance criteria rather than one author representation. Retain only exact identifiers required by the test interface, remove the prescribed design/type/constraint answers from the task prompts, and let stable public feedback identify an unmet criterion without printing SQL. If some mapped objectives are not actually elicited after that change, narrow lab.json objectives rather than overclaiming coverage.

findings.claim: The five lab tasks are one-line answer specifications followed by one shared Test section. They do not give each hands-on task the required four-part numbered procedure—where to look, learner action, expected public feedback, and the observable completion criterion—so a beginner must infer the edit/run/retry loop and which output marks each stage complete. The README also gives no clean way to restart schema.sql from the shipped starter after experimentation.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite each task as a short numbered four-part procedure that names starter/schema.sql and the relevant area, asks for the acceptance-criterion change without revealing SQL, tells the learner to run the one declared command and what failing-test feedback to expect, and names the relevant test passing as completion. Preserve retry and cleanup directions, and add a safe restart-from-starter instruction.
